questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I really wanted to explore the city of Vienna.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I generally really liked the experience and thrived in Vienna. The only downside was figuring out a different system.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: It was a little bit difficult to figure out the system and how to registrer as a resident in the city.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: There was an introduction by the Erasmus team at the university but some of the information was given a little late in relation to the deadlines of the municipality.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: I found housing through google-ing student dorms in Vienna. I lived at a student dorm which belonged to the organisation ÖJAB and I stayed at the house Burgenland 2. I would generally recommend it as it had a nice location and was fairly cheap.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: That there is quite a difference in the different bezirks or neighborhoods in terms of both lived life and distance to campus.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: It seemed that there were a lot of options.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: The registration of arrival at the university was pretty easy as we were given the needed information via e-mail in due time.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: We had a specifically appointed coordinator who was concerned with our field of study and I found that she was able to answer most questions and help.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I found the system a little difficult as there was a lot of prioritizing and practicalities to take into account. Further I had some difficulty as a non-German speaker as there was a limited amount of English courses.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Be open to not getting the courses you want and be open to trying the available English courses.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: It was quite good but had a limited amount of English speaking courses which limited the options a lot.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: The level was all right but it was clear that a lot of the other students were not doing 30 ects points at the same time and that the lecturers expected a little more work due to this.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: Similar but a lot more participation from the students than what I was used to.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
VO Introduction to Urban Sociology
VO Political Sociology
SE Digital Visuality and Popular Culture (P4)
SE Writing and representing in Science and Technology Studies
SE STS, Borders and Mobility
Imagining mobility
Reading Seminar: What is Power? Approaches in Social Theory

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I liked the courses in the STS department as it introduced me to a whole new way of doing social science.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: There were quite a few fees related to registration at the municipality.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Drinks and living was generally okay however I was surprised of the prices of food being similar to Danish. Further I was surprised at how expensive the museums and cultural experiences were. However there were also a lot of free options available and organized by the city.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I found the city to be beautiful and full of lide.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: There was a gym but I did not use it.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Definetely take the time to research the free cultural opportunities in the city as there are many and the museums are very expensive. There are a lot of open air concerts and movie theatres. Further I would recommend checking out all the cafes and nice flee markets in the different areas.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Go to flee markets and try swimming in the Donau Kanal in the sommertime.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Very easy.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Going to bars and be open.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: There were not many differences really. Maybe the use of cash and the fact that a lot is closed on sundays.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The cafe culture and the free cultural opportunities organized different places in the city.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
1. Be aware of the bureaucracy and that it takes time.
2. Experience the cafe culture in the different neighborhoods. 
3. Be sure to visit the old campus at Uni Wien

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: It is nice to rent a bike and then be able to ride around the city and get around very easily.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Getting to experience the city.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: The different registrations and bureaucracy in general.

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer:
Vienna is a very great city! I would totally recommend going there!!! 

And make sure to experience the Wiener Symphoniker at some of their free concerts.

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
